gloss: sir (a respectful term of address to an older man)
glosses: sir (a respectful term of address to an older man)
etym: Inherited from Chagatai اکا (äkä⁠), from Proto-Turkic *āka (“(older) brother”). Compare Uyghur ئاكا (aka), Southern Altai ака (aka), Yakut аҕа (ağa), Tatar агай (ağay), Bashkir ағай (ağay), Kazakh әке (äke), аға (ağa), ағай (ağay), Kyrgyz а
Inherited from Chagatai رَحْمَت (rḥmt), from Classical Persian رَحْمَت (rahmat, “mercy”), from Arabic رَحْمَة f (raḥma, “mercy”).

Inherited from Chagatai قوللوق (qwllwq /⁠qulluq⁠/, “slavery; thank you”). Synchronically analysable as qul (“slave”) + -lik (noun suffix), but fossilised with an obsolete variant of the suffix. Doublet of qullik (“slavery”).
Inherited from Chagatai شکر (škr), from Arabic شُكْر (šukr).

gloss: honorific (before name and traditionally with ezafe)
glosses: honorific (before name and traditionally with ezafe)
etym: Inherited from Chagatai حضرت (ḥżrt), from Arabic حَضْرَة (ḥaḍra).
Borrowed from Arabic لُطْفًا (luṭfan), adverbial accusative of لُطْف (luṭf). By surface analysis, lutf + -an. Compare Turkish lütfen.
Inherited from Chagatai خاکسار (xāksār) from Classical Persian خاکسار (xāksār)
